claims.text: A graph-neural-network neural network potential trained on ab initio molecular-dynamics data can better represent atomic configurations in multicomponent high-entropy-alloy liquids than TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed NNP would reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The NNP is to be trained on ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Training and model selection will use mean-squared-error minimization and Bayesian optimization.
The proposed method applies to alloys containing three to six principal elements.
Principal elements are defined as elements present above 5 at.%, while the stated applicable concentration range is 10–30 at.% per element.
The applicable temperature range is 0.8–1.2 times the melting temperature.
Liquid short-range order is represented by atomic arrangements within the first coordination shell.
Liquid medium-range order is represented by atomic arrangements within the second and third coordination shells.
Short- and medium-range order can be assessed using pair-correlation functions and cluster analysis.
A GNN can learn hierarchical representations of atomic environments and thereby capture complex many-body interactions and configurations.
More accurate prediction of the free-energy landscape will enhance reference–target phase-space overlap and reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
Thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will be reduced by at least 25% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The hypothesis is to be falsified if mismatch reduction is less than 20% or if the free-energy-curve difference exceeds 10 meV/atom.
